name: Benicio Aranda
languages: Spanish (his first language, the Spanish of Monterey)
Enough Portuguese to swear in, from an Azorean whaler's crew
equipment: Leather duster, sun-faded from four summers on the box, over a short Californio jacket with silver buttons he has had to sell two of
Navy revolver (Colt 1851 pattern, .36, cap-and-ball), 5 chambers loaded and the hammer down on an empty one, in a cross-draw holster
A spare loaded cylinder for the Navy, wrapped in a greased rag in his coat pocket (it counts against his .36 rounds when he swaps it in)
Coach gun (a muzzle-loading 12-bore double with the barrels cut to twenty inches), both barrels loaded with buckshot
The shells are paper cartridges of powder and buckshot he rolls himself, kept in a tin box
A tin of percussion caps, a powder flask and a capper on a thong round his neck
Bowie knife with a horn grip
Horse: Ceniza, a grey Californio gelding with a white blaze, who will stand for gunfire and will not stand for mules
A Beaverhead Express Company messenger's badge, brass, and a letter of employment signed by Simeon Prothero, agent at Ninebark
Will Danforth's spurs, which Will's sister sent back to him from the Salt Lake office with a note he has not been able to finish reading
Saddle, saddlebags, bedroll, a buffalo robe for the box in winter, a canteen that freezes
features: Both Sides of the River (Borderlands origin: he speaks English and Spanish natively; among Californio, Mexican and Sonoran packers, muleteers and miners from Hangtown to the Boise Basin he can always find someone who knows his family or knows of it, and has advantage on Persuasion and Insight with them)
Quick Draw (Gunslinger: advantage on initiative and on the draw in a showdown; he draws a Sidearm as part of rolling initiative; drawing and holstering never costs him an interaction)
Gun Hand: Fast Hands (Gunslinger: he reloads a revolver as a bonus action, two rounds, and swaps a spare cylinder as a bonus action; this is why he carries one)
Fan the Hammer (Gunslinger, 2nd level: he can fan up to 4 rounds in one action, the first without disadvantage; fanned shots add no ability modifier to damage)
Style: Duelist (Gunslinger, 3rd level: in a showdown he wins ties on the draw, and if his one shot in the draw round hits it deals an extra weapon damage die)

The Mail Road (Stage Driver background: he has ridden the box on the Bannack and Salt Lake roads; he knows every swing station, every bad grade and every place road agents wait; station keepers and hostlers feed him and tell him who rode through; he can drive any team in ordinary conditions)

personality.traits: I sit quiet and watch the road, the way a man on the box learns to. I am polite to everyone and familiar with no one. I sing in Spanish to the horses when I think no one is listening.
personality.ideals: A man who takes the company's wages guards what is in the box, and the people on the seats, with his life. That is the bargain. The bargain does not include hanging anyone.
personality.bonds: Will Danforth rode messenger with me for two years. On the third of November he went down the grade in my place because I had the fever, and he did not come back. I will find the man who shot him, and I will bring him to a judge, because Will would have.
personality.flaws: I am angrier than I let anyone see. When the committee asked for messengers to stand guard at the hanging I almost said yes. If they ask again with the right name, I do not know what I will say.

appearance: A lean, dark-eyed Californio of twenty-eight with a narrow face, a clipped black moustache and black hair worn a little long under a flat-crowned grey hat. Duster, jacket with silver buttons, a red silk sash under the gun belt that his mother gave him in Monterey. Stands very still and looks at the road behind you.
backstory: Benicio Aranda was born in Monterey in 1836, when it was the capital of Mexican California, and was ten when the flag changed. His father lost the family's land grant to lawyers and squatters in the 1850s, the slow way, one court case at a time, and Benicio left for the mines with a string of mules at nineteen. He packed freight to the Fraser River, to the Comstock, and in 1862 to the Boise Basin, where he went to work for an express company as a messenger: the man who rides the box beside the driver with a shotgun across his knees and the treasure box under his boots. In 1864 the Beaverhead Express Company hired him away to ride the Ninebark to Bannack road. Its coaches were robbed on 13 October and 20 October; on 3 November, with Benicio in bed with a fever, his partner Will Danforth rode in his place and was shot dead on the Rattlesnake Grade. Benicio is back on the box now. He has watched the vigilance committee hang two men, and he does not believe either of them killed Will. (Suggested hook: the party rides in on his coach on Monday 14 November, and Simeon Prothero hires them to ride with him on Thursday's down coach.)
